title: stacked-eviction-thresholds-and-heap-slice-saturation-notes
content:
Purpose:
This note collects field observations, quick experiments, and proposed mitigations for a recurring class of OOMs we saw on multi-tenant GPU pools in Nov–Dec 2024. The failure mode is not a single leak but a combination of: stacked eviction thresholds across layers, small-chunk saturation inside heap slices, and cudaMalloc retry windows that mask transient pressure and exacerbate allocation amplification. The goal here is to capture reproducible signals, simple repros, and low-risk mitigations we can try on Dedicated pools.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Symptom: bursts of OOMs during sustained mixed-size inference traffic (chat + embeddings) with many short lived small allocations (~256B–64KB) and occasional large KV cache growths (>=1MB).
- Root cause (composite): allocator slab/slot fragmentation + conservative eviction thresholds at two layers (serving runtime eviction and pool-level eviction) lead to heap "slice" saturation: lots of free-but-non-contiguous memory that cannot satisfy certain allocation patterns. cudaMalloc retries hold the allocation longer (waiting for async frees/evictions) and amplify tail latency reducing opportunities for direct reuse.
- Short-term mitigations: (1) reduce per-container eviction threshold gap (align pool <-> runtime thresholds), (2) increase workspace headroom by 8–12% for risky instance types, (3) enable deferred coalescing of freed small blocks at end of request.

Incident timeline (abridged):
2024-11-12 03:10 UTC: customer service alerts for 3 QPS endpoints returning 503.
2024-11-12 03:14 UTC: SRE confirms pod-level OOMs on 4/24 GPUs in pool-us-west2-dedicated-04.
2024-11-12 03:20 UTC: Telemetry capture enabled (malloc traces, cudaFree times, slab occupancy series).
2024-11-12 03:45 UTC: Rolling restart of affected nodes prevented immediate recurrence but root cause unclear.

What we observed (telemetry highlights):
- Allocation shape during the incident (sampled 60s window):
  * allocations_count: 78k
  * size distribution (approx): 0–512B: 48% | 513B–64KB: 38% | 64KB–1MB: 10% | >1MB: 4%
- Peak resident GPU memory: 78.9 GB of 80 GB device (NV100-80GB).
- Fragmentation gap estimate (resident vs usable contiguous): successful large allocation failures indicated ~6–10 GB unusable due to fragmentation.
- cudaMalloc retry pattern: majority of failing allocations observed a retry window of 180–220ms during which repeated cudaMalloc attempts returned ENOMEM and finally succeeded only after eviction pulses. Those retries increased tail latency for the owner requests.
- Slab heatmap: hot slabs (small buckets) had 92% occupancy; large contiguous arenas had 30% utilization but were broken into many stranded holes due to 4KB-aligned sloting (internal fragmentation).
- Eviction behavior: runtime-level eviction triggered at 85% resident; pool-level eviction (K8s/cgroup or our pool manager) started reclamation only at 92% device-level resident.

Hypotheses and reasoning: 
H1 — Threshold stacking: The two-layer eviction policy (runtime at 85% and pool daemon at 92%) creates an operating band where the runtime believes "we can still allocate" and defers aggressive coalescing/eviction, while pool-level actions are delayed. When a sudden big allocation is needed, there's insufficient contiguous space.
H2 — Small-chunk saturation: A heavy tail of small allocations pins many slab pages with fragmentation that cannot be coalesced quickly due to per-request free timing and the allocator's freelist policy (LIFO per thread).
H3 — cudaMalloc retry masking: cudaMalloc retry/backoff holds callers in a retry loop; while it waits, more small allocations may arrive, further occupying stray gaps and making the eventual large allocation fail.

Quick repro (lightweight):
- Environment: single 80GB GPU, same allocator build, run mixed worker that performs: 3000 small allocations (random 128–32K) per second, and occasional 8 allocations of size 16–48MB at random intervals (~every 10s).
- Repro script (pseudocode):
  for i in 0..N:
    spawn thread: for j in 0..3000: alloc(random_small); free(maybe after 5–30ms)
    every 10s: alloc(32MB) -> observe success/fail and timing
- Observation: deterministic failure of large alloc after ~30–90s as small-slot occupancy patterns emerge.

Experiments run (notes):
E1 — Align thresholds: lowered pool eviction trigger from 92% to 88% and observed 70% drop in OOM events on a 48h canary. Tail latency improved because fewer cudaMalloc retry windows occurred.
E2 — Deferred coalescing: implemented a cheap coalescer that runs at request boundaries instead of immediate free coalescing. Result: reduced immediate fragmentation and decreased contiguous unusable region estimates by ~40% in synthetic runs.
E3 — Small-block batching: modified allocator to batch small frees and return them to slab head on a timer (10ms window). This reduced allocation amplification but increased peak resident by ~2% due to delayed reclamation.
E4 — Reserve headroom: increased workspace reservation for chat-heavy instances by +10% (configurable per-instance-type). Immediate reduction in observed OOMs, but 6% decrease in overall GPU utilization for the trial pool.

Detailed measurements (representative):
- Baseline (before changes): OOMs per 24h on pool: 4.6 average.
- After E1 (align thresholds): 1.3 OOMs per 24h.
- After E2 (deferred coalescing): large contiguous holes dropped from 9.4GB -> 5.6GB.
- After E3 (small-block batching): failure-to-succeed retry window median dropped from 210ms -> 90ms.

Interpretation: 
- The primary trigger is the time between when reclaimed memory becomes contiguous and when it is usable for a large allocation. Stacked thresholds extend that window. Our allocator's freelist and slot allocation policy contribute heavily to micro-fragmentation under high small-allocation churn. cudaMalloc's retry/backoff behavior is a multiplier, not a root cause.

Low-risk mitigations to try quickly (prod canary):
1) Align eviction thresholds: make runtime eviction more aggressive or make pool-level eviction react earlier (target band: runtime 82–86%, pool 88–90%).
2) Configure per-instance reserve: for instance shapes known to serve mixed workloads (chat+embed), add a workspace buffer option (+8–12%).
3) Enable deferred coalescing at request boundary (flagged off by default).
4) Shorten cudaMalloc retry windows and add a jittered backoff so retries do not synchronize with periodic evictions.

Longer-term mitigations / engineering work: 
- Allocator improvements: introduce compacting free-list passes for small-slab coalescing during low-load windows. Consider per-gpu background defragmenter that can migrate cold tensors and coalesce.
- Adaptive bucket sizing: detect high small-allocation churn and temporarily re-bucket small sizes to reduce internal fragmentation.
- Better visibility: surface contiguous-free-region estimates in Console (per-node heatmap) and expose fragmentation alerts/auto-remediation playbooks.
- Kernel / CUDA knobs: evaluate cudaMallocAsync tuning (if enabled) and interaction with cuMemPool APIs; better to use cuMemPool where we can control coalescing.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q1: How much of the fragmentation is caused by our KV cache eviction policy versus transient request allocations? Need allocation-level labeling and span traces.
- Q2: Can we instrument contiguous-free-region estimates cheaply across devices without heavy sampling?
- Q3: Evaluate memory migration costs for a background compactor — will migration overhead defeat benefits?

Action items (owners):
- Ava: run 72h canary with aligned thresholds across three pools (us-west2,dedicated-04, eu-central-02). Due 2025-01-20.
- Ravi: prototype request-bound deferred coalescer, PR for review (infra repo). Due 2025-01-15.
- Elena: add contiguous-free-region metric to node telemetry (simple estimator) and dashboard. Due 2025-02-01.
- Tom: run perf test to measure cudaMalloc retry window sensitivity with different backoff configs. Due 2025-01-12.

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intended as an operational/engineering working note — not an exhaustive design doc. If we converge on mitigations, we'll draft a formal runbook and a Confluence design that enumerates the allocator changes and safety gates for rollout.

Appendix (quick command snippets):
- capture short alloc trace: MALLOC_TRACE=1 ./binary --alloc-trace > alloc.trace
- sample fragmentation (toy): nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used --format=csv && ./probe_contiguous_allocs 32MB 8
- small repro tool: tools/mem-stress/mixed_workload --small-rate=3000 --large-interval=10s --seed=42

Logs and artifacts: stack traces and malloc traces uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-telemetry/alloc-traces/2024-11-12/

End of note.
